Subject: Escalation: NorthStar reserved throughput shock — exec approval requested

Team —

Pasting the customer email below. NorthStar (DEAL-1284) is observing sustained tail latency and rising 5xx across their reserved capacity (RSVD-22471). Timeline: ~08:45 PDT onset; tokens errors ~0.9% at peak; backend queue depth correlates with a spike in competing non-reserved workloads starting ~08:30.

Quick diagnostics (ops/metrics pulled at 09:24):
- Dedicated pool utilization: 96% GPU-side token processing utilization; scheduler queue depth at 4.8x baseline; KV cache hit-rate down 12% vs last week.
- Top contributors: two non-reserved routes (internal research jobs) consuming short-lived but high-concurrency streams causing eviction churn.
- Impact: customer p50 increased ~13x; p99 > 6s; retry storms visible in request logs.

Proposed immediate mitigation (actionable now):
1) Emergency overflow authorization — allow +20% burst capacity on the Dedicated pool for up to 2 hours. Cost estimate: ~$6,500 one-off for burst nodes.
2) Temporary hosted fallback — shift 12% of NorthStar production traffic to hosted routes for up to 3 hours while we stabilize. Operations will track token counts; recommended customer credit: 5–8% prorated for any hosted overage.
3) Throttle internal non-reserved research jobs and pin kernel selection to reduce eviction churn (ops).
4) Post-mortem: incident bridge + root-cause within 48 hours; customer-facing timeline and SLA credit proposal prepared by CS.

Decision requested: approve emergency overflow (option 1) and approve preliminary customer credit (option 2). We need an exec go/no-go to avoid a longer customer outage — NorthStar is a mid-enterprise account running payment reconciliation during the morning window.
